title: Sterling Bowles and Warren Easton alumni
summary: Discussion of trumpeter Sterling Bowles, his possible daughter and wife, and another Easton trumpeter who went to Hollywood.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: They were all, for the most part, Warren Eastern people, weren't they? I would say yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. Did you know Sterling Bowles?
I did not, no. That's a name to me. Yeah, well, one of the guys that was here, I can't remember his age. You know, there are so many people that you hear talking about.

Oh, these were all standard names. In other words, I knew about Sterling Bowles when I was just a young kid. I mean, a kid in the music business, I was 16, 17 years old, but I don't think I ever met him. As a matter of fact, to the best of my memory, he died as a fairly young man.
How old was he when he died? I don't remember. I think he died in the 1950s or 60s. Well, I didn't know him. But he left town very early, and he was making records,

I guess, while you were at Warren Eastern. I think his daughter is still a member of the local here. I don't know about that. Yes. I think her name is Mary Hugh. I'd have to look it up to be sure, but Sterling Bowles, if this is the one I'm talking about, was married to a harpist.
I don't remember. He was a big band trumpet player.

I might, yes. I'm pretty sure I'm right. I might be a little cloudy, but my name was Lavedan. She always used her maiden name. And Lucienne Lavedan, who played with the operands, she used to do some of the things with the symphony. I'm fairly certain that they had been married, and this girl would have been the daughter of that union. I think he went to Warren Easton. I think
Luke Skiro just told me about Warren Easton and different people he knew there. There's so many
of them that were there. Well, Bowles wouldn't have been younger than I. He would have been older. Get older, yeah. Sure. So I don't know how Luke could have known him. I knew Luke.
Oh, no, I'm just saying through the years I picked up the names associated with Warren Easton,

and I think Luke went there. I'm trying to, you were talking about Easton, I'm trying to remember the name of the guy who left as a young man, a trumpet player, who went to Hollywood, Los Angeles, and for years he was the standard first trumpet man on nearly all the motion picture soundtracks. He had a German name. Something like Schlegel. Wade Schlegel, sure. I remember Wade.
There could be some confusion there. Oh, sure. Well, no, there's just a million names.
